subject: ela
intro: These exercises focus on using pronouns correctly. For each item, read the short sentence, then choose the correct pronoun or name the pronoun type. Each sentence has its antecedent named and nearby, so you have everything you need right in the item.

items.prompt: Read the sentence: 'My brother and (I / me) walked to the store after dinner.' Which pronoun correctly completes the sentence?

steps: Find the verb and ask who is doing the action. 'My brother and ___ walked' tells you the pronoun is part of the subject.
Subjects use the subjective case: I, he, she, we, they.
Test it alone: 'I walked to the store' is correct, but 'Me walked to the store' is not.
The correct pronoun is 'I'.

items.prompt: Read the sentence: 'Coach Lee gave the new uniforms to Tara and (I / me).' Which pronoun correctly completes the sentence?

steps: The pronoun comes after 'to', so it is part of the object that receives the action.
Objects use the objective case: me, him, her, us, them.
Test it alone: 'Coach Lee gave the uniforms to me' is correct, but 'to I' is not.
The correct pronoun is 'me'.

items.prompt: Read the sentence: 'The teacher praised (we / us) for finishing the project early.' Which pronoun correctly completes the sentence?

steps: The pronoun receives the action of the verb 'praised', so it is an object.
Objects use the objective case: me, him, her, us, them.
'The teacher praised us' is correct; 'praised we' is not standard English.
The correct pronoun is 'us'.

items.prompt: Read the sentence: '(She / Her) and Marcus organized the entire fundraiser.' Which pronoun correctly completes the sentence?

steps: The pronoun is part of the subject performing the action 'organized'.
Subjects use the subjective case: I, he, she, we, they.
Test it alone: 'She organized the fundraiser' is correct; 'Her organized' is not.
The correct pronoun is 'She'.

items.prompt: Read the sentence: 'Mr. Diaz handed the awards to Jordan and (they / them).' Which pronoun correctly completes the sentence?

steps: The pronoun follows 'to' and receives the action, so it is part of the object.
Objects use the objective case: me, him, her, us, them.
'Mr. Diaz handed the awards to them' is correct; 'to they' is not.
The correct pronoun is 'them'.

items.prompt: Read the sentence: 'The principal herself handed out the diplomas at graduation.' What type of pronoun is the word 'herself' in this sentence?
items.answer: An intensive pronoun (it emphasizes the noun 'principal')

steps: Find the word 'herself' and see what it adds to the sentence.
It does not receive the action; it sits right after 'principal' to stress that the principal personally did the action.
A pronoun that emphasizes a noun in this way is called an intensive pronoun.
So 'herself' is an intensive pronoun emphasizing 'principal'.

items.prompt: Read the sentence: 'I built the birdhouse myself without any help.' What type of pronoun is the word 'myself' in this sentence?
items.answer: An intensive pronoun (it emphasizes the subject 'I')

steps: Look at the word 'myself' and what it does in the sentence.
It adds emphasis, stressing that 'I' did the building alone, and can be removed without changing the basic meaning.
A pronoun that emphasizes another noun or pronoun is an intensive pronoun.
So 'myself' is an intensive pronoun emphasizing 'I'.

items.prompt: Read the sentence: 'The students themselves chose the theme for the dance.' What type of pronoun is the word 'themselves' in this sentence?
items.answer: An intensive pronoun (it emphasizes the noun 'students')

steps: Locate 'themselves' and check its job in the sentence.
It comes right after 'students' and stresses that the students, not anyone else, made the choice.
A pronoun used to emphasize a noun is an intensive pronoun.
So 'themselves' is an intensive pronoun emphasizing 'students'.

items.prompt: Read the sentence: 'Devon and (I / me) studied together for the science quiz.' Which pronoun correctly completes the sentence?

steps: The pronoun is part of the subject doing the action 'studied'.
Subjects use the subjective case: I, he, she, we, they.
Test it alone: 'I studied for the quiz' is correct; 'Me studied' is not.
Avoid the common 'Me and Devon' error. The correct pronoun is 'I'.

items.prompt: Read the sentence: 'Please save a seat for (he / him) at the assembly.' Which pronoun correctly completes the sentence?

steps: The pronoun follows 'for' and is the object of that word.
Objects use the objective case: me, him, her, us, them.
'Save a seat for him' is correct; 'for he' is not standard English.
The correct pronoun is 'him'.

items.prompt: Read the sentence: 'Is this backpack (your / yours)?' Which pronoun correctly completes the sentence?

steps: The sentence asks who owns the backpack, so it needs a possessive pronoun.
'Your' must come before a noun (your backpack), but here no noun follows.
When a possessive stands alone at the end, use 'yours': 'Is this backpack yours?'
The correct pronoun is 'yours'.

items.prompt: Read the sentence: '(We / Us) cheered loudly when the team scored.' Which pronoun correctly completes the sentence?

steps: The pronoun is the subject doing the action 'cheered'.
Subjects use the subjective case: I, he, she, we, they.
'We cheered loudly' is correct; 'Us cheered' is not standard English.
The correct pronoun is 'We'.

items.prompt: Read the sentence: 'Aunt Rosa gave (she / her) a ride to practice.' Which pronoun correctly completes the sentence?

steps: The pronoun receives the action of the verb 'gave', so it is an object.
Objects use the objective case: me, him, her, us, them.
'Aunt Rosa gave her a ride' is correct; 'gave she a ride' is not.
The correct pronoun is 'her'.

items.prompt: Read the sentence: 'The cat cleaned itself after the long nap.' What type of pronoun is the word 'itself' in this sentence?
items.answer: A reflexive pronoun (it receives the action and refers back to 'cat')

steps: Find 'itself' and see whether it emphasizes a noun or receives the action.
Here the cat both does and receives the cleaning, so 'itself' is the object of 'cleaned' and points back to 'cat'.
A pronoun that receives the action and refers to the subject is a reflexive pronoun. If you removed it, the sentence would change meaning.
So 'itself' is a reflexive pronoun referring to 'cat'.

items.prompt: Read the sentence: 'My friends and (I / me) packed snacks for the field trip.' Which pronoun correctly completes the sentence?

steps: The pronoun is part of the subject performing the action 'packed'.
Subjects use the subjective case: I, he, she, we, they.
Test it alone: 'I packed snacks' is correct; 'Me packed snacks' is not.
The correct pronoun is 'I'.
